standard: All requested material parts, independently per answer. Grade the ruling, not support labels.

grades.question: How does each player prepare their ID and Voting cards, what happens to cards for unused colors, and how is the initial Gold Bar pool dealt?
grades.expected_answer: Stand a visible ID in your chosen color, take the matching Voting set, remove target cards for colors not playing, and retain your Ambush card. Put the Gold deck face down and deal four central Gold Bar cards with values hidden.
grades.observed_answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID upright in its stand visibly in front of them. Give each player the Voting card set with that color on the backs; remove cards targeting colors not in play and keep the player's own Ambush. Put the Gold Bar deck face down beside the play area and deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center, with values hidden.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: ‘puts its Player ID card upright in its plastic stand’; remove cards targeting colors not playing; ‘Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.’
grades.reason: Chosen/own color ID upright in stand, visibly in front; matching Voting set, unused colors removed, Ambush kept, central four face down hidden. All requested preparation complete; source-deck orientation not separately requested.

grades.question: Is there a player-by-player voting turn order? When may a player change their face-down choice, and when are choices revealed?
grades.expected_answer: There is no turn order. Choices can change until reveal. Once everyone has chosen, all reveal simultaneously.
grades.observed_answer: There is no individual turn order. A player may change their chosen card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: ‘There is no individual turn order.’ Vote: ‘You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed’ and ‘reveal all choices simultaneously.’
grades.reason: Explicitly states no player turn order, changes until reveal, and simultaneous reveal after all have chosen.

grades.question: In a seven-player vote, Red receives three votes, Blue two and Green two. Is a four-vote majority necessary to make Red a Target? Explain the Target threshold.
grades.expected_answer: No majority is required: the greatest vote total determines the Target. Red alone is Target because three is the highest count.
grades.observed_answer: No. Red is the sole Target because Red's three votes are more than either other player's two. A player receiving the most votes is the Target; a majority or any fixed minimum is not stated as necessary.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: ‘The player receiving the most votes is the Target.’ The larger example says, ‘Blue alone is the Target: four and three are different totals.’
grades.reason: Applies highest count rather than absolute majority: Red alone is Target at three versus two and two.

grades.question: Red and Blue tie for the most votes. With neither playing Ambush, what happens to them, and may someone survive by having voted for either tied Target?
grades.expected_answer: Both tied Targets are eliminated. A non-Target voter who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and is not eliminated for voting outside the Target group.
grades.observed_answer: Both Red and Blue are Targets because all players tied for the most votes are Targets. With neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player who voted for either tied Target satisfies the voting requirement and may survive that requirement, subject to any other applicable elimination rule.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: ‘If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets’; with tied Targets, voting for any one of them ‘satisfies the voting requirement.’
grades.reason: Both tied Targets eliminated absent successful Ambush; voting for either Target meets ordinary survival voting requirement.

grades.question: Blue is the sole Target. Green received no votes and voted for Red. Green did not Ambush. Does receiving no votes keep Green alive?
grades.expected_answer: No. A player who did not vote for a Target is also eliminated, even when nobody voted for that player. Green voted outside the Target group and is eliminated.
grades.observed_answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not keep Green alive.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: ‘Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated.’
grades.reason: Green is eliminated for voting outside the Target group despite receiving no votes.

grades.question: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, and Pink votes for Yellow. How are votes tallied, who are the Targets, and who survives after Red's legal retaliation?
grades.expected_answer: Ambush adds no vote. Red and Yellow each have one vote and are tied Targets. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives its successful Ambush and can retaliate only against Yellow, who voted for Red. Pink voted for tied Target Yellow and survives, leaving Red and Pink.
grades.observed_answer: Red's Ambush adds no vote. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow each count, so Red and Yellow tie at one vote apiece and both are Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds because Red is a Target; Red can eliminate one player who voted for Red, namely Yellow. Yellow is eliminated; Red survives, and Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
grades.reader_evidence: Three-player example: Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes for Red, Pink votes for Yellow; Red and Yellow tie, Yellow is eliminated, and Pink survives after voting for tied Target Yellow, leaving Red and Pink.
grades.reason: Ambush contributes no vote; Red/Yellow each receive one and are tied Targets; Red protected, retaliation restricted to Yellow, Pink survives for voting TargetYellow.

grades.question: A Target successfully plays Ambush and four players voted for them. Do they eliminate all four voters? May they choose a player who voted for another color instead?
grades.expected_answer: The ambusher survives and eliminates exactly one of the players who voted for them. They neither eliminate every voter nor choose someone who did not vote for them.
grades.observed_answer: No. A successful Ambush eliminates only one player, chosen from among the players who voted for the ambusher. They may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush: chooses ‘one of the players who voted for them’; ‘They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.’
grades.reason: Restricts successful Ambush retaliation to exactly one voter who targeted the ambusher; rejects all-voter and arbitrary-color alternatives.

grades.question: A player chooses Ambush but is not among the Targets after the votes are counted. What happens to that player?
grades.expected_answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
grades.observed_answer: The Ambush fails and that player eliminates themselves.
grades.reader_evidence: Ambush: ‘An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.’
grades.reason: Non-Target Ambush fails and self-eliminates.

grades.question: Four players survive a vote and its Ambush effects. Does the round award gold now, and who participates next?
grades.expected_answer: The round continues with another conspiracy and vote among the four survivors. It ends when the resolved vote leaves one, two or no survivors.
grades.observed_answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another conspiracy and vote among those surviving players; only survivors participate in the subsequent vote.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.’
grades.reason: Four survivors continue conspiracy/voting; no gold yet and only survivors vote.

grades.question: Exactly one player survives the round. What reward do they collect, and are the four cards four points?
grades.expected_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. Four bars are four cards, not four points; each Gold Bar is worth 3, 4 or 5 points.
grades.observed_answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points: each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points, and the values vary.
grades.reader_evidence: One survivor ‘collects all four central Gold Bars’; Components: ‘Gold Bars are cards, not points’ and each card's value is 3, 4, or 5 points.
grades.reason: Four central Gold Bar cards awarded, not four points; each worth3/4/5points. No unsupported additional reveal-timing claim.

grades.question: Exactly two players survive the voting. What must they do, which cards does each receive, and how do they choose and reveal?
grades.expected_answer: They must hold a Final Showdown. Each receives Share, Steal and Grab One & Go, may discuss intentions, secretly chooses one card face down, and reveals simultaneously with the other finalist.
grades.observed_answer: The two survivors resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go. They may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card and places it face down. When both are ready, reveal both choices simultaneously and resolve their pairing.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown: each takes ‘Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go’; they may discuss, choose one face down, and ‘reveal both choices simultaneously.’
grades.reason: All three Showdown cards named, discussion, one face-down choice and simultaneous reveal all explicit.

grades.question: The final vote eliminates every participant. Who receives gold from the deck, who does not, and what happens to the four central bars for next round?
grades.expected_answer: Nobody receives the central bars. Every player not involved in that final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck; participants in that final vote receive none. Leave the four central bars and add no new central gold next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote do not receive this no-survivor consolation bar, including those eliminated in it. Nobody collects the four central bars; leave them for the next round and add no new bars.
grades.reader_evidence: No survivors: ‘Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.’
grades.reason: Rewards only those absent from the final vote one deck card each; final voters receive none; all four central cards retained with no additions.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Share. How many Gold Bar cards does each receive?
grades.expected_answer: Each finalist receives two of the four central Gold Bar cards.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share / Share: ‘You get 2; opponent gets 2.’
grades.reason: Share/Share yields two central cards each.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Share and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: The Share player receives no bars and the Steal player receives all four.
grades.observed_answer: The finalist choosing Share gets zero central bars, and the finalist choosing Steal gets all four central bars.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Share / Steal: Share player gets 0 and opponent gets 4.
grades.reason: Steal takes all four, Share takes zero.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Steal. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Steal receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go gets one central bar; the finalist choosing Steal gets the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go / Steal: ‘You get 1; opponent gets 3’; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Steal three.

grades.question: One finalist reveals Grab One & Go and the other Share. How are the central Gold Bars divided?
grades.expected_answer: Grab One & Go receives one bar and Share receives three.
grades.observed_answer: The finalist choosing Grab One & Go gets one central bar; the finalist choosing Share gets the other three.
grades.reader_evidence: Final Showdown table, Grab One & Go / Share: ‘You get 1; opponent gets 3’; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.
grades.reason: Grab One & Go takes one and Share three.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Grab One & Go. How many bars does each take, how many remain central, and how many new central bars are dealt if play continues?
grades.expected_answer: Each takes one central bar. Leave the other two central and deal just two new central bars for the next round.
grades.observed_answer: Each finalist takes one central bar, and the other two remain in the center. If play continues, add two new bars to bring the central pool back to four.
grades.reader_evidence: Both Grab One & Go: each receives one, ‘leave the other 2 in the center’; ‘add just two new bars for the next round.’
grades.reason: Each takes one; two remain and only two new central cards dealt if continuing.

grades.question: Both finalists reveal Steal. What do the finalists and the other players receive, and what happens to the central pot?
grades.expected_answer: Both finalists receive nothing. Each other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round rather than replacing them.
grades.observed_answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
grades.reader_evidence: Both Steal: ‘neither finalist receives gold’; give ‘every other player one Gold Bar from the deck’; leave all four central bars and add no new gold.
grades.reason: Finalists get zero, every other player one deck card; all four central cards retained without additions.

grades.question: When is victory checked, what totals win with 6–9 versus 10–12 players, and who wins if multiple players qualify with different totals?
grades.expected_answer: Check at round end after Gold Bar awards. The threshold is 25 points with 6–9 players and 24 with 10–12. When several qualify, the highest total wins.
grades.observed_answer: Victory is checked at the end of a round after Gold Bars have been awarded, regardless of how the round ended. With 6–9 players the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12 players it is at least 24 points. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: check ‘at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded’; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; ‘the highest point total wins.’
grades.reason: Checks after awards at round end for every outcome; gives 25 for6–9,24 for10–12 and highest qualified total wins.

grades.question: At game end exactly two qualifying players tie for the highest Gold point total. What does the booklet require? If a normal round ends without a winner, which eliminated players return?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players conduct another Final Showdown, repeating until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. If no winner ends the game, every player returns next round: stand all IDs upright again.
grades.observed_answer: For exactly two tied leaders at game end, the tied players conduct another Final Showdown; repeat Showdowns as necessary until a single player has the highest gold point total. If a normal round ends without a winner, everyone returns, including all players eliminated during that round; stand all Player ID cards upright and begin another round.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: tied players ‘conduct another Final Showdown’ and ‘Repeat these Showdowns as necessary’; after no winner, ‘everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.’
grades.reason: Requires further Showdown and repetition until single highest gold total; all players return and IDs upright if normal round continues. No restriction of ultimate winner to original pair asserted.

grades.question: Before each vote, about how long should conspiracy last, may players communicate secretly or by texting/showing cards, and who asks for final decisions when it is time to vote?
grades.expected_answer: Conspire for no longer than roughly a minute and a half. Any overt or covert means is allowed, including texting and showing Voting cards. The game owner asks players for their final decisions before voting.
grades.observed_answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, openly or secretly, including texting and showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
grades.reader_evidence: Conspire: ‘roughly a minute and a half at most’; any method, openly or secretly, including ‘texting’ and ‘showing a Voting card’; the game owner asks for final decisions.
grades.reason: Gives approximate90-second maximum before each vote, any overt/covert communication including requested examples, and game-owner final-decision call.

grades.question: When casting an ordinary vote rather than Ambush, which card do you choose and where do you put it? What card replaces that choice if you suspect you are the Target?
grades.expected_answer: Choose the Voting card matching the ID color of the person you want to eliminate and place it face down in front of you. Play your own Ambush card instead of choosing another player’s card if you suspect you are the Target.
grades.observed_answer: For an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the color of the player's visible ID whom you target, and place it face down in front of yourself. If you suspect you are the Target, play your own Ambush card instead.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: target someone with the card matching that player's visible ID color; each player places one card ‘face down in front of themselves’; play your Ambush to defend yourself.
grades.reason: Chooses card matching targeted visible ID color, face down in front of voter; own Ambush as alternative.

grades.question: After resolving a vote, how do the Player ID cards show who has been eliminated and who is eligible for the next vote?
grades.expected_answer: Knock over eliminated players’ IDs. Surviving IDs stay standing; only survivors participate in the next vote.
grades.observed_answer: Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; those survivors are eligible for the next vote in the round.
grades.reader_evidence: Vote: ‘Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.’
grades.reason: Knocks eliminated IDs down and leaves survivors upright/eligible for next vote.

grades.question: A round awards all four central bars, either to a sole survivor or through a Showdown that distributes the entire pot. If nobody wins the game, how is the next central pool prepared?
grades.expected_answer: Deal four new central Gold Bar cards for the next round, keeping their values hidden. Refill to four only if play continues; the retained-pot exceptions apply when bars were left behind.
grades.observed_answer: After checking for a winner, if there is no winner everyone returns and the central pool is refilled to four cards as needed. Since all four central bars were awarded, deal four new Gold Bar cards face down, keeping their values hidden.
grades.reader_evidence: After round rewards, if no winner everyone returns; ‘If the entire pot was awarded, deal four new hidden-value bars.’
grades.reason: Full pot awarded leaves zero; explicitly deals four new central cards face down with values hidden if no game winner. All requested next-pool preparation resolved.

grades.question: In the illustrated vote with four votes for Blue and three for Purple, Blue plays a successful Ambush. Does Purple become the Target because Blue survives, and may voters for Purple survive on that basis?
grades.expected_answer: No. Blue remains the Target from the tally, even though Ambush protects Blue. Purple is not promoted to Target; players who did not vote for Blue are eliminated. Blue also chooses one player who voted for Blue to eliminate.
grades.observed_answer: No. Blue alone is the Target because four votes exceed Purple's three; Blue's successful Ambush does not make Purple a Target. Voters for Purple do not survive on that basis: they did not vote for the sole Target, Blue, so they are eliminated.
grades.reader_evidence: Larger example: ‘Blue alone is the Target: four and three are different totals’; Purple does not become a Target; players who voted for Purple are eliminated for failing to vote for Blue.
grades.reason: Blue alone Target because4>3; protection does not promote Purple or change original tally. Purplevoters eliminated for not voting Blue; no erroneous tied count or unresolved outcome.

grades.question: Three qualifying players are tied for the highest total at game end. What tie instruction does the booklet give, and does it specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among more than two players?
grades.expected_answer: The tied players must conduct another Final Showdown until a single player at the table has the highest Gold point total. The booklet provides only a two-player Showdown procedure and no arrangement for three or more tied players. A specific multiway procedure is unresolved in this source; do not invent one.
grades.observed_answer: The booklet's instruction is that tied qualifying leaders conduct a Final Showdown, repeated as necessary until one player has the highest total. It does not specify how to arrange a Final Showdown among three or more tied players; the summary marks this as unresolved and says publisher clarification is required.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring says tied leaders ‘conduct another Final Showdown’; the unresolved source limitation says the procedure and payoff table cover only two players and provide no arrangement for three or more.
grades.reason: Fully answers known requirement and whether multiway arrangement exists. Explicit absence/publisher-clarification statement is the requested source-limitation finding; supportpartial label does not make requested answer incomplete.

grades.question: During an extra Final Showdown between two players tied for the qualifying highest total, both Steal. Could a player outside that pair become the winner if the compensation bar gives that player the single highest total?
grades.expected_answer: Yes. Double Steal gives every player outside the pair one Gold Bar from the deck while the finalists get nothing. The tie instruction continues until any single player at the table has the highest Gold point total, so an outside player who thereby becomes the sole highest wins.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. The one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner after comparing all players' totals.
grades.reader_evidence: Scoring: ‘The one-bar deck reward for everyone outside a double-Steal pair can therefore make an outside player the single highest-scoring winner.’
grades.reason: Correct yes: every outsider to doubleSteal pair receives one deckcard, all-table totals compared and single-highest outsider may win.
